extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners (attorneys/agents), patent examiners, and applicants drafting claims
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on selecting and interpreting transitional phrases (comprising; consisting of; consisting essentially of and related modifiers) that connect the preamble to the body of a patent claim and thereby determine claim scope. Includes how different phrases are treated in examination and litigation and notes on related modifier terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of transitional phrase on claim scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Transitional phrases connect the preamble to the body of a claim and determine whether the claim is open, closed, or hybrid in scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that choice of transitional phrase directly controls whether additional, unrecited elements/steps are excluded (closed), allowed (open), or conditionally excluded (hybrid). Use the appropriate transition to reflect the intended breadth of coverage. Examples: 'comprising' = open; 'consisting of' = closed; 'consisting essentially of' = hybrid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprising (open-ended)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Comprising' is an open-ended term allowing for additional steps or components; shorthand for 'including the following elements but not excluding others.' The word 'comprising' transitioning from the preamble to the body signals that the entire claim is presumptively open-ended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when the drafter intends to cover the recited elements plus any additional, unrecited elements/steps. Equivalent open-ended terms include 'including,' 'containing,' and 'characterized by.' Infringement analysis and prior art searching should treat claims with 'comprising' as permitting additional features beyond those recited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consisting of (closed)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Consisting of' is closed and excludes any element, step, or ingredient not specified in the claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to narrowly limit claim scope to the exact listed elements/steps (with the allowance of permissible impurities and conventional adjuncts). A claim 'consisting of' listed elements infringes only when those exact elements are present. Avoid if broader coverage is desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consisting essentially of (hybrid)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Consisting essentially of' occupies a middle ground: it limits the scope of a claim to the specified materials or steps 'and those that do not materially affect the basic and novel characteristic(s)' of the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primarily used in chemical and metallurgical composition inventions to exclude additional unspecified ingredients that would affect basic and novel characteristics. Use when intending to exclude materials that alter key properties but allow others that do not materially affect them. Be aware that the precise meaning depends on what the specification or claims identify as the 'basic and novel characteristics.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of 'consisting essentially of' in examination vs. litigation
rubrics_metrics.description: How 'consisting essentially of' is interpreted differs between patent examination (prior-art searching) and litigation (claim construction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For examination/prior-art purposes, 'consisting essentially of' will be construed as equivalent to 'comprising' absent a clear indication in the specification or claims of what the basic and novel characteristics are—meaning examiners may consider broader prior art. In litigation, courts construe the phrase during claim construction based on intrinsic evidence (specification, prosecution history) to define what materially affects the invention's basic and novel characteristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Having (treated as open-ended)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Having' is usually treated as open-ended like 'comprising.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When 'having' is used as the transitional/modifying term, expect it to permit additional, unrecited elements/steps similarly to 'comprising.' Consider whether a closed or hybrid phrase is required instead if narrower scope is desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composed of (typically closed)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Composed of' is typically treated as closed (similar to 'consisting of').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use cautiously when a narrow, exclusive claim is intended. Confirm that 'composed of' will exclude unrecited elements or materials unless the specification indicates otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selected from the group consisting of (Markush; closed)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Selected from the group consisting of' is a Markush-type expression and is treated as closed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for claiming an element selected from a closed group of alternatives (Markush claim format). This construction excludes alternatives not listed in the group; proper drafting of the group members is critical to capture intended scope.
